answer: Each identity runs one marble slab stack in a vault yard and locks a 70 credit bond. Each epoch a sparrow flight photographs the stack and files its image hash in the ledger. An auditor recounts slabs, checking height, edges, and seal marks. A mismatch, reused photograph, or moved seal burns the bond. The first filing costs 28, the kth 28+5(k-1), the 1000th 5023; 1000 false identities pay 2,525,500 plus 70,000 locked, sharing no photograph. A rented-stack ring fails because seal marks belong to one stack only. An honest operator pays 28 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
